Package com.j3d.engine.interact.input.keyboard

Class J3Key

java.lang.Object
com.j3d.engine.interact.input.keyboard.J3Key
public class J3Key extends Object
A singular key on the keyboard or keystroke that gets put into KeyBindings. A J3Key can be identified within KeyBindings.getActionMap() or KeyBindings.getInputMap() via it's UUID.

This can either be a keystroke to do one task, which can have its action switched out for something else temporarily. Say if you have some key which works on W and you'd like to switch it to work for something else and then switch it back to normal.

A J3Key can also represent a one shot key where it deregisters itself after clicking.

A J3key can also be linked to other keys. See GlobalKeybinds.SELECT_SUBTRACT_DOWN for example which is the leader of a 4 keychain link. If it's I keybind is changed, the children will also change along with their own respective keycode. e.g. if I changes to G+SHIFT, and it was linked to I+CTRL, that will change to the new parent's code plus the child's original modifiers G+SHIFT+CTRL. In a chain the leader's KeyEvent is what will cascade and not a child's parent. It is vital that if you use linking, the parent node (often referred to in these docs as the leader) should not be identical to any other child node. See KeyBindings.childModifiersClash(J3Key) however to summarise, a leader keyStroke's AWTKeyStroke.getModifiers() AND AWTKeyStroke.isOnKeyRelease() cannot clash with any one of the children defined within the chain.
